acceptance_criteria.text: Guides 8 and 20 are removed from the catalogue, a repository rule prevents guides with undrawn pieces from landing, and tests catch violations of that rule

body.facts:
Retire guide 8, "What does the progress bar show?", and guide 20, "What if a step changes a file it never said it would?" — no screen draws either piece any more. Take them out of the catalogue, and add a repository rule that every guide's piece is drawn somewhere, so this can't happen again. https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/1718

Guide 8 is in the catalogue with no piece on screen

Guide 8, *What does the progress bar show?*, is in the catalogue and openable from Guides, and nothing on a Job opens it. Its only mark was on the run tree, which no longer exists.

## What happened

`GuideMark guide={GUIDE_STEP_BAR}` is drawn in `packages/screens/src/InsideAJob.tsx:379`, and nothing renders `InsideAJob` since the Overview reframe of 29 September 2026. So the guide's piece, `run.step-bar`, is on no screen.

The guide describes a bar that no longer exists in the form it describes:

> The run is the workflow's steps, in the order this job runs them… A bar carries one segment for each piece of work under it… The mark beside the step is what says the work is still running.

## What is missing

A decision has already been taken: asked whether to bring it back or retire it, the owner chose **retire**. Nothing has been done about it since.

So either the guide comes out of the catalogue, or what remains true of it moves to a piece that is drawn. Worth checking before deleting: the Plan card's group rows and the Workflow canvas both draw progress, and *the bar never moves on its own* may still be a thing worth saying about one of them — in which case this is a rewrite against a new piece rather than a removal.

## In

`packages/components/src/guides/008-what-does-the-progress-bar-show.ts` and `guides/index.ts`. `GUIDES` is walked by `guides-met.ts` and by the catalogue, and the numbering is stable — read what removing a number does to both before doing it.

## What proves it

`guides.test.tsx` was retargeted from `GUIDE_STEP_BAR` to `GUIDE_WORKFLOW` on 30 September, because guide 8 could no longer be the first piece a person meets on a Job. That change records the problem; this issue is the part that was left.

**There is no gate for this.** A guide in the catalogue whose piece no screen draws passes everything, which is the same family as https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/1668 and https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/1678 — two other gaps found by eye this week. A rule that every guide's `piece` is drawn somewhere would have caught it the moment the reframe landed, and is worth considering as part of this.

spec.spec: xtask/src/rules_guides/tests.rs — Rust unit tests for the rule. The `test` and `desktop_test` checks passed on this branch; `desktop_test` had failed once on a studios.test.tsx timeout (not touched by this change) and passed on rerun with no code change.

specs.spec: xtask/src/rules_guides/tests.rs — Rust unit tests for the rule. The `test` and `desktop_test` checks passed on this branch; `desktop_test` had failed once on a studios.test.tsx timeout (not touched by this change) and passed on rerun with no code change.

xtask/src/rules_guides/tests.rs — Rust unit tests for the rule (undrawn fails, drawn passes, catalogue-only exempt, story/test/index mention doesn't count, prefix name isn't a match). The workspace `test` check passed after the last fix.

Register it in xtask/src/main.rs, give it Rust unit tests with fixture trees (undrawn piece fails, drawn passes, catalogue-only exempt, a mark only in a story or test does not count), and document it where the guides contract lives in docs/contracts/design-system.md (and docs/INDEX.md if a new doc is added). body.name: bug
body.for_requests: Something that is broken: it used to work, or is meant to work, and does not, and what is wanted is the cause found and fixed. Taking a change that already landed back out whole is a revert, and adding or changing what the software does on purpose is a feature.

body.name: code_review
body.for_requests: A pull request somebody wants reviewed: a link to one, where the code is already written and what is wanted is a judgement on it rather than a change to it.

body.name: design_plan
body.for_requests: Working out how something should be built before anybody builds it: a design or plan drafted, then revised with whoever asked until they are content, where the result is a document and no code is written. Trying the idea out in code is a prototype.

body.name: epic
body.for_requests: Finishing a milestone or an epic: a link to one, or a list of issues somebody wants done as a whole, which is too much for one change and has to be split into several Jobs that run in turn.

body.name: feature
body.for_requests: Adding, removing or changing what the software does or shows: a new screen, option or command, a change to how something behaves, or taking away something people could see or use, meant to land and stay. Fixing something broken is a bug, and moving code around while nothing anyone sees changes is a refactor.

body.name: prototype
body.for_requests: Trying something out to answer a question: a spike or rough version built to see whether an idea works, shown to whoever asked and written up, then thrown away rather than landed. Something meant to ship is a feature, and a design worked out on paper is a design plan.

body.name: refactor
body.for_requests: Reorganising code without changing what it does: moving, renaming, splitting or tidying, where nothing anyone can see or use changes -- no screen, no output, no behaviour. A request that adds, removes or changes anything a person sees or can do, however small, is a feature and not a refactor.

body.name: revert
body.for_requests: Undoing a change that already landed: the commit or Job the request names, taken back out whole and nothing else with it. Keeping the change and fixing what it broke is a bug.

> The run is the workflow's steps, in the order this job runs them… A bar carries one segment for each piece of work under it… The mark beside the step is what says the work is still running.

Guide 8 is in the catalogue with no piece on screen

Guide 8, *What does the progress bar show?*, is in the catalogue and openable from Guides, and nothing on a Job opens it. Its only mark was on the run tree, which no longer exists.

## What happened

`GuideMark guide={GUIDE_STEP_BAR}` is drawn in `packages/screens/src/InsideAJob.tsx:379`, and nothing renders `InsideAJob` since the Overview reframe of 29 September 2026. So the guide's piece, `run.step-bar`, is on no screen.

The guide describes a bar that no longer exists in the form it describes:

> The run is the workflow's steps, in the order this job runs them… A bar carries one segment for each piece of work under it… The mark beside the step is what says the work is still running.

## What is missing

A decision has already been taken: asked whether to bring it back or retire it, the owner chose **retire**. Nothing has been done about it since.

So either the guide comes out of the catalogue, or what remains true of it moves to a piece that is drawn. Worth checking before deleting: the Plan card's group rows and the Workflow canvas both draw progress, and *the bar never moves on its own* may still be a thing worth saying about one of them — in which case this is a rewrite against a new piece rather than a removal.

## In

`packages/components/src/guides/008-what-does-the-progress-bar-show.ts` and `guides/index.ts`. `GUIDES` is walked by `guides-met.ts` and by the catalogue, and the numbering is stable — read what removing a number does to both before doing it.

## What proves it

`guides.test.tsx` was retargeted from `GUIDE_STEP_BAR` to `GUIDE_WORKFLOW` on 30 September, because guide 8 could no longer be the first piece a person meets on a Job. That change records the problem; this issue is the part that was left.

**There is no gate for this.** A guide in the catalogue whose piece no screen draws passes everything, which is the same family as https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/1668 and https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/1678 — two other gaps found by eye this week. A rule that every guide's `piece` is drawn somewhere would have caught it the moment the reframe landed, and is worth considering as part of this.

This is done when:
  - Guides 8 and 20 are removed from the catalogue, a repository rule prevents guides with undrawn pieces from landing, and tests catch violations of that rule

THE PLAN

Approach: Retire guides 8 and 20 the way guide 11 was retired: delete their files, drop them from the imports, exports and GUIDES array in guides/index.ts, and add 8 and 20 to RETIRED_GUIDE_NUMBERS so numbers stay stable (the existing guides.test.ts number-accounting tests then hold with the new retired set). Before deleting, check the two candidates for a rewrite: Plan card group rows and the Workflow canvas draw progress, but the owner already chose retire for 8, and guide 20's piece run.drift has no GuideMark anywhere, so both are removals. Guide 8's only mark is GuideMark guide={GUIDE_STEP_BAR} in packages/screens/src/InsideAJob.tsx:379, so remove that mark and its import. The 'step-bar' GuideFigureId and its StepBars drawing in GuideFigure (and its story) exist only for guide 8, so remove them too; leave the StepBar component, which other screens use. Then add the repository rule as an xtask gate rule in the style of rules_stories.rs (no TS parser, read the one shape a guide file has): for every guides/NNN-*.ts, read the exported const name and `piece`, and require the const to be referenced by a GuideMark/guide prop in a non-story, non-test source under packages/ or apps/, except the five catalogue-only pieces decided in guide.ts (job.what, job.before, plan.what, run.drone, workflow.what), which the rule names as an explicit list. Register it in xtask/src/main.rs, give it Rust unit tests with fixture trees (undrawn piece fails, drawn passes, catalogue-only exempt, a mark only in a story or test does not count), and document it where the guides contract lives in docs/contracts/design-system.md (and docs/INDEX.md if a new doc is added). Part 3 adds the vitest side: guides.test.ts asserts 8, 20 and 11 are retired and absent. After the change, run guide 8/20 searches in docs/concepts for prose that now points at them.
